| [CLAIM-432](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-432.md) v2 | A corporation can be an agent fit to be held responsible and the bearer of functional affect in Frijda's sense, so psychopathy's affective features can be assigned to it as well as its conduct: it lacks remorse, functionally, when harm it does to others is not among the concerns its own appraisals track and gains precedence over what it does only when a regulator or a market turns it into a threat to the corporation's concerns; that profile, threat without remorse, is the construct's, and it is changed by redesigning the corporation's concerns, not its members' characters | The record's reading of Bakan's "institutional psychopath", filed at the owner's request on 2026-10-23 and revised the same day when the owner pointed out that the record's framework assigns affect to corporation-like things ([CLAIM-039](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-039.md), reopened). On Frijda's account an emotion is an appraisal of an event's pertinence to a concern, eliciting action readiness with control precedence; a corporation has concerns, appraisals and readiness. A harm to others reaches its decisions either as one of its own concerns (procedures, role duties: functional concern and remorse) or as a threat to its other concerns (regulators, markets: functional fear). A corporation with only the second is functionally psychopathic across the construct, not in part. Wells Fargo's sales practices ([CASE-151](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-151.md)) are its documented case. | Proposed |
